actions.description: Advance the simulated world by a bounded number of fixed timesteps, optionally applying an action for each step, and return the resulting observation and terminal flags.

inputs.description: Transitions to advance; the action is applied at every tick
inputs.name: ticks

inputs.description: The action applied at each tick, shaped by the environment's action space
inputs.name: action

actions.name: step

actions.description: Reset the simulated world to a scenario start state and return the initial observation. When a seed is supplied the endpoint records it in the receipt; otherwise the endpoint's declared default seed applies.

inputs.description: Seed of the environment's random generator
inputs.name: seed

actions.name: reset

actions.description: Set the seed used by the simulated world's random number generators for subsequent steps, without resetting the world. The accepted seed is echoed in the receipt.

inputs.name: seed

facts.text: The action space is a Box with low -1 and high 1 shaped by the ACTIONS list
ACTIONS lists six absolute arm joints and then the normalized gripper position (0 close, 1 open), for the left arm and then for the right arm
The control timestep DT is 0.02 and FPS is 50; the comment on the DT line derives 50 hz from it
The simulation's control timestep is that DT, passed to the dm_control Environment as control_timestep

The observation of obs_type pixels_agent_pos is a Dict of a nested pixels Dict whose top member is a uint8 Box of 0 to 255 shaped observation_height x observation_width x 3, and an agent_pos Box between -1000.0 and 1000.0
observation_width defaults to 640 and observation_height to 480
The observation image is rendered 480 high and 640 wide from the top camera
The gripper observation is the finger position normalized by normalize_puppet_gripper_position, so 0 is closed and 1 is open
The start qpos is waist 0, shoulder -0.96, elbow 1.16, forearm roll 0, wrist angle -0.3, wrist rotate 0 and fingers 0.02239 and -0.02239 for each arm
reset(seed) seeds the task's random generator and replaces its numpy RandomState with RandomState(seed)
The object poses are drawn uniformly: the peg x from 0.1 to 0.2, the socket x from -0.2 to -0.1, both y from 0.4 to 0.6 and both z from 0.05 to 0.05
step returns terminated = is_success = (reward == 4), truncated False and an info carrying is_success
The InsertionTask reward is 1 when both grippers touch peg and socket, 2 when neither object touches the table, 3 when the peg touches a socket and 4 when the red peg touches the pin
The TransferCubeTask reward rises from 1 to 4 with the right gripper, the lift, the left gripper and a transfer that leaves the table
AlohaInsertion-v0 registers AlohaEnv with max_episode_steps 300, obs_type pixels and task insertion, and AlohaTransferCube-v0 registers the same class with task transfer_cube
Both registered environments set nondeterministic True because even after seeding the rendered observations are slightly different
The state observation type is not implemented: obs_type state raises NotImplementedError

determinism.notes: reset(seed) or cap.world.seed.v1 fixes the object poses through a numpy RandomState(seed) (gym_aloha/utils.py:9 and :24) and the joint dynamics of MuJoCo are deterministic, so one implementation repeats a trajectory for the same seed and actions; the upstream registers nondeterministic True because the rendered images still differ slightly (gym_aloha/__init__.py:7-9), and this package's fake draws with Python's random.Random instead of numpy's generator, so a seed gives different poses on the two

gaps: MuJoCo rigid-body physics of two ViperX arms in the scenes of gym_aloha/assets: no contacts, no friction, no actuator, sensor or noise model, and no camera physics

the fake backend does not integrate any dynamics: the commanded joint targets and the unnormalized gripper positions become the state, so the contact-based reward (gym_aloha/tasks/sim.py:174-219) is always 0 and a success (reward 4) can never be observed there

the fake backend returns a 4 x 6 x 3 stand-in image where the environment renders 480 x 640 x 3 (gym_aloha/tasks/sim.py:92); that stand-in is a uniform colour derived from the seeded peg pose, it is not a picture of the scene
no wall-clock pacing: realtime_factor 0, ticks advance simulated time by timestep_ms (DT 0.02 s, gym_aloha/constants.py:4) only
snapshot and restore are not offered: AlohaEnv exposes no get_state or set_state

the fake backend was not compared with the upstream environment (gym_aloha was not importable where the gate ran), its object poses come from Python's random.Random instead of numpy's RandomState, and its action is a list where AlohaEnv asserts a one-dimensional numpy array (gym_aloha/env.py:174)

measures.description: Last observation (derived from the observation space)
measures.name: observation

safe_state.description: the simulation stops advancing: no step, reset or seed is accepted after an e-stop until mhs.safety.reset clears the latch; the environment state is kept and stays readable
